name: Dify
summary: Open-source LLM application platform providing a visual workflow canvas, RAG knowledge bases, agent nodes, and a plugin marketplace, served by a self-hostable Docker Compose stack with PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery workers, a pluggable vector database, and a sandbox service. Applications publish as web apps, REST APIs, MCP servers, or reusable tools.
license: Dify Open Source License (Apache-2.0 with added conditions)

agent-runtime.note: Runs chat, agent, and workflow applications server-side with function-calling and ReAct agent strategies, persisting conversations and run records.

orchestration.note: Visual workflow canvas with multi-node pipelines plus schedule, webhook, and plugin trigger nodes.

knowledge-memory.note: Built-in RAG pipeline covering document ingestion, embedding, and retrieval, backed by a configurable vector database such as Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, or pgvector.

tools-integration.note: Ships 50+ built-in tools with hundreds of model providers, MCP server publishing, HTTP request nodes, and webhook triggers, extensible through the plugin marketplace.

identity-governance.note: Workspaces have Owner/Admin/Editor/Normal roles with per-knowledge-base visibility, but audit log and enterprise governance are not in the Community Edition.

observability.note: Per-run logs with node-by-node traces, token totals, and status, plus integrations with external tools such as Langfuse, Opik, and Arize Phoenix.

data-secrets.note: Managed file storage via OpenDAL, S3, Azure Blob, or GCS, with a server key encrypting session tokens and stored provider credentials.

evaluation.note: No dataset, scorer, or eval-run subsystem; quality tooling is limited to logs and manual annotation.

channels.note: Applications publish as a hosted web app chat UI, while Slack, Telegram, and Discord bots require marketplace or custom plugins rather than a built-in gateway.

code-execution.note: The Code node runs Python or JavaScript in the DifySandbox service, an isolated environment with a syscall whitelist blocking file, network, and shell access.

human-in-loop.note: The Human Input node pauses a workflow and emits an event carrying a form token, delivers a form via web app or email, routes execution by the decision taken, and follows a timeout branch.

multi-tenancy.note: Workspaces isolate apps, knowledge bases, members, and model configuration under four roles, but the self-hosted Community Edition gets one workspace and multiple workspaces require Enterprise.

declarative-deployment.note: Dify DSL exports one app's configuration to YAML and recreates it on import with a compatibility check, but there is no dependency graph, plan/apply, or multi-resource provisioning.

agent-versioning.note: A version control panel publishes drafts as named versions and restores previous ones, but offers no aliases, canary rollout, traffic splitting, or eval-gated promotion.

skill-learning.note: Apps, workflows, tools, and knowledge bases are authored by humans in the studio; no mechanism has the agent create or refine reusable skills from its own runs.
